claims.text: Molybdenum can be used as an interlayer between W and CuCrZr.
A thin molybdenum interlayer improves the stability of the W/CuCrZr interface under fusion reactor conditions.
A molybdenum interlayer mitigates thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
A molybdenum interlayer limits interdiffusion between W and CuCrZr.
An untreated W/CuCrZr interface is prone to interdiffusion.
The thermal-expansion mismatch at an untreated W/CuCrZr interface causes mechanical degradation.
A 100–500 nm molybdenum film deposited by physical vapor deposition is a suitable interlayer configuration for W/CuCrZr.
The deposited molybdenum layer will form a continuous, homogeneous barrier.
A continuous molybdenum layer acts as a diffusion barrier at the W/CuCrZr interface.
A continuous molybdenum layer accommodates differential thermal expansion between W and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum has a coefficient of thermal expansion intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum is chemically inert in the proposed W/Mo/CuCrZr interface and operating environment.
Molybdenum's intermediate thermal expansion and chemical inertness reduce interfacial thermal stress and interdiffusion.
Reduced interdiffusion and thermal stress maintain joint integrity under extreme conditions.
W/Mo/CuCrZr will have greater mechanical stability than a direct W/CuCrZr bond under comparable fusion-relevant conditions.
W/Mo/CuCrZr will exhibit less interfacial degradation than a direct W/CuCrZr bond.
The molybdenum interlayer will extend component service life.
The effectiveness of the molybdenum interlayer may diminish above approximately 1200 °C.
Discontinuities caused by fabrication defects may diminish the effectiveness of the molybdenum interlayer.
